title: RAG, Part 3: Hybrid Search and Measuring Quality

scenes.text: Your RAG chatbot works in the demo. [1] But then a user types an exact order number, and it finds nothing useful. [2] Today, in RAG part three, we fix that with hybrid search, and learn how to measure if RAG is actually good.

There are two ways to search. [1] Keyword search matches exact words. It's great for names, codes, and order numbers. [2] Semantic search matches meaning. It's great when people use different words for the same idea. [3] Each one misses what the other catches.

Hybrid search runs both at the same time. [1] Keyword search finds the exact matches, [2] semantic search finds the meaning matches, [3] and the results are merged into one ranked list, before reranking.

data.definition: Running keyword search and semantic search together, then merging their results into one ranked list.

scenes.text: Here's a quick example. [1] For the question, order 4 5 8 1 status, keyword search wins. [2] For, my parcel hasn't shown up, semantic search wins. [3] Hybrid gets both right.

Now, how do we know if RAG is good? [1] First, retrieval. Did it find the right chunks? This is called recall. [2] Second, faithfulness. Does the answer stick to those chunks, without making things up? [3] Third, relevance. Does the answer actually address the question?

Here's how teams test it. [1] Build a golden set, real questions with known correct answers. [2] Run every question through the RAG system. [3] Score each answer, using people, or another AI as a judge. [4] Change one thing, like chunk size. [5] Run it again, and compare the scores.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think if a few demo questions look right, the RAG system is ready. [2] A demo is not a test. Real users ask messy, surprising questions. Measure with a golden set, before you launch.

data.myth: If a few demo questions look right, it's ready to launch.
data.fact: Real users ask messy questions. Measure with a golden set before launch.
data.tip: A demo is not a test

scenes.text: Quick quiz! A user searches an exact product code. Which search is most likely to find it? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] Keyword search, because it matches exact words and codes. Hybrid search gives you both!

Let's recap. [1] Keyword search matches exact words. [2] Semantic search matches meaning. [3] Hybrid search combines both. [4] And we measure retrieval, faithfulness, and relevance, with a golden set. [5] Next, open versus closed AI models. Follow AI Maastaaru!
